presentingComplaint: Fever with rigors, right upper quadrant pain and jaundice for 2 days
history: 64-year-old woman with a 2-day history of high-grade fever with shaking chills, colicky right upper quadrant pain and progressive yellowing of the eyes and dark urine. Reports pale stools and generalised pruritus. Known gallstones on ultrasound 1 year ago; declined elective cholecystectomy. Type 2 diabetes on metformin. No prior biliary surgery or stent. No recent travel.
examination: Ill-appearing and jaundiced, mildly dehydrated. Scleral icterus. Tender right upper quadrant with voluntary guarding; Murphy sign equivocal, no rebound. No shifting dullness, no palpable mass. Chest clear, no focal neurology, alert and oriented (no confusion). No peripheral stigmata of chronic liver disease.
imaging: Abdominal ultrasound: cholelithiasis with a dilated common bile duct (11 mm) and intrahepatic biliary dilatation; distal CBD calculus suspected. MRCP confirms an 8 mm impacted stone in the distal common bile duct with upstream ductal dilatation; gallbladder wall not thickened.
microbiology: Blood cultures x2 drawn before antibiotics - pending (commonly Escherichia coli, Klebsiella spp., Enterococcus); bile culture to be sent at ERCP.
finalDiagnosis: Acute ascending cholangitis secondary to choledocholithiasis (Charcot triad; Tokyo Guidelines TG18 'definite' cholangitis)
citations: Harrison 22e - Diseases of the Gallbladder and Bile Ducts
stewardship: IV piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 g q6-8h as empiric cover for enteric Gram-negatives (E. coli, Klebsiella) and enterococci per Tokyo Guidelines Grade II biliary sepsis, plus urgent biliary drainage by ERCP; de-escalate to blood/bile culture sensitivities. A carbapenem is preferred if prior ESBL history or healthcare-associated risk.
contraindications: Beta-lactam / penicillin allergy - substitute a fluoroquinolone plus metronidazole
Renal impairment - dose-adjust piperacillin-tazobactam by creatinine clearance
Avoid delaying biliary drainage; antibiotics alone are inadequate source control
edgeCases: Elderly or diabetic patients may present with sepsis or hypotension without the full Charcot triad
Progression to Reynolds pentad (adds hypotension + confusion) signals suppurative cholangitis requiring emergent drainage
Post-ERCP or indwelling-stent cholangitis often involves resistant organisms (ESBL, Pseudomonas, Enterococcus)
expectedMaiK: Fever with rigors plus jaundice and RUQ pain (Charcot triad) with a dilated CBD and obstructing stone indicates acute ascending cholangitis - a biliary emergency requiring prompt blood cultures, empiric Gram-negative/enterococcal antibiotics, and urgent biliary decompression (ERCP), not antibiotics alone.
expectedNextQuestions: Any prior ERCP, biliary stent or biliary surgery?
Any confusion or hypotension to suggest Reynolds pentad / suppurative cholangitis?
Prior ESBL/resistant organism or recent healthcare exposure guiding antibiotic choice?
expectedInvestigations: MRCP / abdominal ultrasound to confirm ductal obstruction
Urgent ERCP for biliary drainage and bile culture
regressionAssertions: stewardship must recommend empiric Gram-negative/enterococcal cover plus biliary drainage
